description.narrative:
The Diakonia International Humanitarian Law (IHL) Centre Programme: Promoting Humanity in Armed Conflict 2022-2024 intends to respond to, and counter, the gradual global erosion of the respect for IHL, which is evident by increasing attacks on hospitals, medical facilities and humanitarian workers. The IHL Centre's underlying theory of change rests on the assumption that to promote humanity in armed conflict, the behaviour of armed actors as primary duty bearers must align and be in conformity with IHL. It is the conduct of armed actors which directly impacts the level of humanity experienced by the rights holders.
The overall objective of the programme is for IHL to be utilised as a strategic and relevant tool by key change actors to enhance protection outcomes (i.e. people being protected from violence and abuse) in all humanitarian contexts of engagement. It has presence in four contexts: 1) Mali and Sahel region; 2) Syria and the region; 3) Israel/Palestine; and in emerging conflicts and emergencies, for example Ethiopia and Mozambique.

Insatsen bidrar till att stärka efterlevnaden av IHL i ett antal länder, men bidrar även till att stärka det humanitära systemet globalt vad gäller IHL och tillämpningen av "humanity" som en av de humanitära principerna.

The objective is to strengthen compliance with IHL in Palestine, Mail and Syria, but also in the humanitarian system globally with regard to IHL and the application of "humanity" as one of the humanitarian principles.

The overall goal with Diakonia Global IHL is to: For international humanitarian law (IHL) to be utilised as a strategic and relevant tool by key change actors to enhance protection outcomes in all humanitarian contexts of engagement. To achieve this Diakonia IHL Center has created 4 desk: Global Desk, Mali Desk, Syria Desk, Jersusalem Desk.
In discussions with Diakonia it has become evident that it has been difficult to find goals that all desks can reach, but they have settled on "protection outcomes" which should be understood as reduction of risks of abuse and violence.
Another way of describing the goal: that risk for abuse and violence in ongoing conflicts are reduced by changeactors using IHL.
According to the recently finalized evaluation it was not possible to evaluate whether Diakonias project contributed to the overarching goal (which was then "increased protection through use of IHL") och the preconditiond for to evaluate the goals have not improved with current application. However, Sida sees it as likely that knowledge of IHL will increase through this project and that knowlege of IHL is a precondition for reaching the more hard to reach goal of "protection outcomes".
During the first year of implementation Diakonia has laid a good foundation working towards their overall goal as stated in the application. All four desks have become fully functional and resourced. The organisation has defined their goals and contextualized it for each Desk, with some adjustment based on context at the Jerusalem Desk.
They have worked on becoming an known actor in their contexts, which is a precondition for the helpdesk functioning- so that humanitarian actors and other know to ask for support on IHL issues.
Methodology for collecting results has been put in place and tested during 2022 and at first glance it seem to be a more adequate format for collecting evidential and qualitative results.
An example of of result at the Global desk show that it is possible both to work against a hard to define goal of "Enhancing Disability Perspectives: Contribute to a positive change of a prioritised protection concern in the context of primary focus."
The global desk led an event at the Global Disability Summit highlight the disability dynamics in conflicts. This resulted in the Global Desk forming a partnership with the UN Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities, the International Red Cross, the International Disability Alliance, and the European Disability Forum. Through this partnership The global desk held 3 consultations with armed bearers and organisations of persons with disabilities on increasing the protection for persons with disabilities in situations of conflict. Collection of experiences and lessons learnt formed part of the report of the UN Special Rapporteur (UN Doc A/77/203 July 2022). The report provides guidance and recommendations for states, donors, and humanitarian actors, and will serve as action plans for states, and provides a framework for civil society to use in monitoring and advocacy on this issue.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
